```{r shared-setup}
#| include: false
#| cache: false
source("scripts/analysis_setup.R")

# APA-style p-values: no leading zero, "< .001" below .001.
format_p_value <- function(p) {
  ifelse(p < .001, "< .001", sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", p)))
}
```

## Rating items

Each participant rated all seven visualizations on four items, each on a 5-point scale.
The comparison item was asked right after Task 1; the other three after Task 2, when
participants had used each visualization in both tasks. Comparisons within an item are
unaffected, but differences between items may partly reflect this timing.

| Item | Label on this page | Survey wording or label | Response scale | Asked |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A301 | Helpful for comparison | "Helpful for comparison" | 1 = very unhelpful … 5 = very helpful | After Task 1 |
| A302 | Helpful for detection and integration | "Helpful for detection" | 1 = very unhelpful … 5 = very helpful | After Task 2 |
| A303 | Would use in publication or presentation | "I would prefer to use this visualization for representing signal mean and standard error in a publication or presentation" (survey label "Usage material") | 1 = very unlikely … 5 = very likely | After Task 2 |
| A304 | Aesthetically appealing | "Appealing" | 1 = very unappealing … 5 = very appealing | After Task 2 |

: Rating items. A303 measures the likelihood of using a visualization, not its helpfulness. A301 was answered right after the comparison task, before participants had seen Task 2. {.striped}

::: {.callout-note title="Limitation: fixed item order"}
Within every rating question the visualizations were listed in the same order for every
participant: Adjacent plots first and Basic topoplot always last. Order and context effects
therefore cannot be separated from differences between visualizations.
:::

## Rating data preparation and descriptive summary

```{r}

question_labels <- c(
  A301 = "Helpful for comparison",
  A302 = "Helpful for detection and integration",
  A303 = "Would use in publication or presentation",
  A304 = "Aesthetically appealing"
)

# All four questions presented the visualization types in the same order.
# The A304 columns retain that order in the export, but their suffixes are
# nonsequential (01, 06, 02, 03, 04, 05, 07).
rating_columns <- list(
  A301 = sprintf("A301_%02d", seq_along(vistypes)),
  A302 = sprintf("A302_%02d", seq_along(vistypes)),
  A303 = sprintf("A303_%02d", seq_along(vistypes)),
  A304 = c(
    "A304_01", "A304_06", "A304_02", "A304_03",
    "A304_04", "A304_05", "A304_07"
  )
)

rating_key <- purrr::imap_dfr(
  rating_columns,
  \(columns, question_code) tibble(
    question_code = question_code,
    rating_column = columns,
    vistype = vistypes
  )
)
```

```{r subjective-rating-validation}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Validation checks"
#| results: hide

if (!identical(names(rating_columns), names(question_labels)) ||
    any(lengths(rating_columns) != length(vistypes)) ||
    anyDuplicated(rating_key$rating_column) ||
    nrow(rating_key) != 28L) {
  stop("The subjective-rating key must contain 28 unique survey columns.")
}

# Validate the explicit key against the question labels embedded in the first
# row of the LimeSurvey export. Stop rather than silently relabel results if the
# questionnaire changes in a future export.
rating_key_validation <- rating_key %>%
  mutate(
    survey_label = as.character(
      unlist(legend[1, rating_column], use.names = FALSE)
    ),
    label_matches = stringr::str_detect(
      survey_label,
      stringr::fixed(vistype)
    )
  )

if (any(is.na(rating_key_validation$survey_label)) ||
    any(!rating_key_validation$label_matches)) {
  stop("The subjective-rating key does not match the embedded survey labels.")
}
```

```{r}
likert <- data %>%
  select(ID, all_of(rating_key$rating_column)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    -ID,
    names_to = "rating_column",
    values_to = "rating_raw"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    rating_key %>% select(rating_column, question_code, vistype),
    by = "rating_column"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    vistype = factor(
      vistype,
      levels = vistypes
    ),

    question = factor(
      question_code,
      levels = names(question_labels),
      labels = unname(question_labels)
    ),

    rating = as.integer(
      stringr::str_extract(as.character(rating_raw), "^-?\\d+")
    ),

    rating = if_else(
      rating %in% 1:5,
      rating,
      NA_integer_
    )
  ) %>%
  select(ID, question, vistype, rating)
```

```{r likert-summary-table}
likert_table <- likert %>%
  group_by(vistype, question) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_rating = round(mean(rating, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = question,
    values_from = mean_rating
  ) %>%
  # Basic topoplot first (the reference), then the survey order. No composite
  # score: the four items measure different things (A303 is likelihood of use)
  # and A301 was asked at a different time, so an equal-weight sum has no
  # clear meaning (audit U10).
  arrange(vistype != "basic", vistype)

likert_table |>
  mutate(vistype = table_vistype(vistype)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 2,
    col.names = c("Visualization type", unname(question_labels)),
    caption = "Mean subjective ratings by visualization type (raw means, 1–5)",
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )
```
## Ordinal mixed-effects models

```{r}
likert_model_data <- likert |>
  filter(!is.na(rating)) |>
  mutate(
    ID = factor(ID),
    vistype = droplevels(factor(vistype)),
    rating_ord = ordered(rating, levels = 1:5)
  )

likert_models <- likert_model_data |>
  (\(data) split(data, data$question))() |>
  map(
    \(data_question) clmm(
      rating_ord ~ vistype + (1 | ID),
      data = data_question,
      Hess = TRUE
    )
  )

likert_estimates <- imap_dfr(
  likert_models,
  function(model, question_name) {

    emmeans(
      model,
      ~ vistype,
      mode = "mean.class"
    ) |>
      confint() |>
      as.data.frame() |>
      transmute(
        question = question_name,
        vistype,
        estimated_rating = mean.class,
        lower_ci = asymp.LCL,
        upper_ci = asymp.UCL
      )
  }
)

likert_estimates |>
  mutate(vistype = table_vistype(vistype)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 2,
    col.names = c(
      "Evaluation criterion",
      "Visualization type",
      "Estimated rating",
      "Lower 95% CI",
      "Upper 95% CI"
    ),
    caption = "Model-smoothed mean ratings",
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

model_table_note(paste0(
  "Separate cumulative-link mixed models with logit link are fitted for each ",
  "evaluation criterion: <code>rating_ord ~ vistype + (1 | ID)</code>. ",
  "Estimated marginal means use <code>mode = &quot;mean.class&quot;</code>: they are ",
  "model-smoothed mean ratings on the 1–5 scale, with asymptotic pointwise 95% ",
  "confidence intervals (not adjusted for multiplicity)."
))
```

### Model checks and sensitivity analyses

```{r likert-model-checks}
#| cache: false
# 1. Proportional odds: fixed-effects clm with and without visualization-specific
#    thresholds (nominal effects), compared by likelihood-ratio test.
po_tests <- likert_model_data |>
  (\(data) split(data, data$question))() |>
  imap_dfr(function(data_question, question_name) {
    po_fit <- clm(rating_ord ~ vistype, data = data_question)
    npo_fit <- clm(rating_ord ~ 1, nominal = ~ vistype, data = data_question)
    lrt <- anova(po_fit, npo_fit)
    tibble(
      question = question_name,
      lr_statistic = lrt$LR.stat[2],
      df = lrt$df[2],
      p_value = lrt$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2]
    )
  })

# 2. Model-smoothed vs raw means.
raw_vs_model <- likert |>
  group_by(question, vistype) |>
  summarise(raw_mean = mean(rating, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(question = as.character(question), vistype = as.character(vistype)) |>
  inner_join(
    likert_estimates |> mutate(vistype = as.character(vistype)),
    by = c("question", "vistype")
  ) |>
  mutate(abs_difference = abs(estimated_rating - raw_mean))
max_raw_model_difference <- max(raw_vs_model$abs_difference)

# 3. Linear mixed model on the 1–5 ratings: same Dunnett contrasts vs Basic.
likert_lmm_contrasts <- likert_model_data |>
  (\(data) split(data, data$question))() |>
  imap_dfr(function(data_question, question_name) {
    fit <- lmer(rating ~ vistype + (1 | ID), data = data_question)
    question_emmeans <- emmeans(fit, ~ vistype)
    set.seed(20261118)  # adjust = "mvt" integrates numerically (Monte Carlo)
    contrast(
      question_emmeans,
      method = "trt.vs.ctrl",
      ref = which(question_emmeans@levels$vistype == "basic"),
      adjust = "mvt"
    ) |>
      confint() |>
      as.data.frame() |>
      transmute(
        question = question_name,
        vistype = stringr::str_remove(contrast, " - basic$"),
        lmm_difference = estimate,
        lmm_lower = lower.CL,
        lmm_upper = upper.CL
      )
  })

po_tests |>
  mutate(p_value = format_p_value(p_value)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 1,
    col.names = c("Evaluation criterion", "LR statistic", "df", "p"),
    caption = paste(
      "Proportional-odds check: fixed-effects cumulative-link model vs a model with",
      "visualization-specific thresholds (likelihood-ratio test)"
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )
```

**Proportional odds.** The likelihood-ratio test rejects proportional odds for
`r sum(po_tests$p_value < .05)` of 4 criteria (p from
`r format_p_value(min(po_tests$p_value))` to `r format_p_value(max(po_tests$p_value))`):
the visualizations differ in how ratings are spread over the scale, not only in their
location. The analysis therefore reports model-smoothed *mean* ratings, which stay close to
the raw means (largest absolute difference `r sprintf("%.2f", max_raw_model_difference)`
scale points), rather than interpreting the odds ratios.

**Random-effects structure.** Each participant gave exactly one rating per visualization and
criterion. Participant-specific visualization effects (`(1 + vistype | ID)`) would have one
observation per random effect and are not identifiable separately from the observation-level
latent error, so the random intercept is the maximal identifiable structure. The linear mixed
model below is a sensitivity check that does not rely on proportional odds.

## Model-estimated ratings

```{r}
#| cache: false
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 11
question_columns <- unname(question_labels)

likert_vistype_order <- c(
  "basic",
  "adjacent",
  "triple_CI",
  "uncert_markers",
  "animation",
  "bivariate_range",
  "bivariate_corner"
)

likert_display_labels <- c(
  basic = "Basic topoplot",
  adjacent = "Adjacent plots",
  triple_CI = "Confidence intervals",
  uncert_markers = "Uncertainty markers",
  animation = "Animation",
  bivariate_range = "Bivariate range",
  bivariate_corner = "Bivariate corner"
)

likert_panel_titles <- c(
  "Helpful for comparison" = "Helpful for comparison",
  "Helpful for detection and integration" = "Helpful for detection & integration",
  "Would use in publication or presentation" = "Would use in publication",
  "Aesthetically appealing" = "Aesthetically appealing"
)

make_likert_estimate_plot <- function(
  question_name,
  show_x = TRUE,
  show_labels = TRUE
) {

  plot_data <- likert_estimates |>
    filter(question == question_name) |>
    mutate(
      colour_group = if_else(vistype == "basic", "basic", "other"),
    
      display_label = unname(
        likert_display_labels[as.character(vistype)]
      ),
    
      vistype = factor(
        vistype,
        levels = rev(likert_vistype_order)
      )
    )

  p <- ggplot(
    plot_data,
      aes(
    x = estimated_rating,
    y = vistype,
    colour = colour_group
  )
  ) +
    geom_errorbar(
      aes(
        xmin = lower_ci,
        xmax = upper_ci
      ),
      orientation = "y",
      width = 0.12,
      linewidth = 0.55
    ) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +

    # Estimated values
    geom_text(
      aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", estimated_rating)),
      nudge_y = 0.32,
      vjust = 0.5,
      size = 30 / ggplot2::.pt
    ) +

    scale_colour_manual(
  values = c(
    basic = "#3B78B4",
    other = "#222222"
  ),
  guide = "none"
) +

    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = 1:5,
      labels = function(x) sprintf("%.0f", x),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.02))
    ) +

    # Hide ordinary y-axis labels
    scale_y_discrete(
      labels = NULL,
      expand = expansion(add = 0.5)
    ) +

    # Show custom labels placed slightly outside the panel
    coord_cartesian(
      xlim = c(1, 5),
      clip = "off"
    ) +

    labs(
      title = unname(likert_panel_titles[question_name]),
      x = NULL,
      y = NULL
    ) +

    theme_classic(base_family = "Lato", base_size = 20) +

    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        hjust = 0.5,
        face = "bold",
        size = 50
      ),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 20),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 20),
      axis.text.y = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      axis.line.y = element_blank(),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),

      # Space for custom labels
       plot.margin = margin(
    t = 5.5,
    r = 5.5,
        b = 8,
    l = if (show_labels) 245 else 12
  )
    )

  if (show_labels) {
    p <- p +
      geom_text(
        data = plot_data,
        aes(
          x = 0.9,
          y = vistype,
          label = display_label,
          colour = colour_group
        ),
        inherit.aes = FALSE,
        hjust = 1,
        size = 14,
        lineheight = 1
      )
  }

  if (!show_x) {
    p <- p +
      theme(
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
      )
  }

  p
}

p1 <- make_likert_estimate_plot(
  question_columns[1],
  show_x = FALSE
)

p2 <- make_likert_estimate_plot(
  question_columns[2],
  show_x = FALSE,
  show_labels = FALSE
)

p3 <- make_likert_estimate_plot(
  question_columns[3],
  show_x = TRUE
)

p4 <- make_likert_estimate_plot(
  question_columns[4],
  show_x = TRUE,
  show_labels = FALSE
)

likert_estimate_figure <-
  (p1 + p2) /
  (p3 + p4) +
  plot_annotation(
    caption = "Model-smoothed mean rating (pointwise 95% CI)",
    theme = theme(
      plot.caption = element_text(
        hjust = 0.5,
        size = 26,
        family = "Lato",
        lineheight = 1.1,
        margin = margin(t = 10, b = 6)
      ),
      plot.caption.position = "plot",
      plot.margin = margin(6, 12, 12, 12)
    )
  )


likert_estimate_figure

ggsave_st(
  project_path("figures", "likert_estimate_figure.png"),
  likert_estimate_figure,
  width = 16,
  height = 11,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 180,
  device = ragg::agg_png,
  bg = "white"
)
```

## Differences relative to Basic topoplot

```{r likert-basic-contrasts}
#| include: false

likert_contrasts <- imap_dfr(
  likert_models,
  function(model, question_name) {
    question_emmeans <- emmeans(
      model,
      ~ vistype,
      mode = "mean.class"
    )

    basic_reference <- which(
      question_emmeans@levels$vistype == "basic"
    )

    set.seed(20261118)  # adjust = "mvt" integrates numerically (Monte Carlo)
    contrast_result <- contrast(
      question_emmeans,
      method = "trt.vs.ctrl",
      adjust = "mvt",
      ref = basic_reference
    ) |>
      confint() |>
      as.data.frame()

    lower_column <- grep(
      "lower.CL$|asymp.LCL$",
      names(contrast_result),
      value = TRUE
    )[1]
    upper_column <- grep(
      "upper.CL$|asymp.UCL$",
      names(contrast_result),
      value = TRUE
    )[1]

    contrast_result |>
      transmute(
        question = question_name,
        vistype = stringr::str_remove(contrast, " - basic$"),
        difference = estimate,
        lower_ci = .data[[lower_column]],
        upper_ci = .data[[upper_column]]
      )
  }
) |>
  group_by(question) |>
  mutate(
    vistype = factor(vistype, levels = rev(likert_vistype_order[-1])),
    # Highlight contrasts whose Dunnett-adjusted interval excludes zero (no
    # "leader": differences between non-reference visualizations are not tested).
    excludes_zero = lower_ci > 0 | upper_ci < 0
  ) |>
  ungroup()

likert_contrast_limit <- max(
  2,
  ceiling(
    max(abs(c(likert_contrasts$lower_ci, likert_contrasts$upper_ci)), na.rm = TRUE) * 10
  ) / 10
)

format_rating_difference <- function(x) {
  ifelse(
    abs(x) < 0.05,
    "0.0",
    sprintf("%+.1f", x)
  )
}

make_likert_contrast_plot <- function(
  question_name,
  show_x = TRUE,
  show_labels = TRUE
) {
  plot_data <- likert_contrasts |>
    filter(question == question_name)

  p <- ggplot(
    plot_data,
    aes(x = difference, y = vistype)
  ) +
    geom_vline(
      xintercept = 0,
      linetype = "dashed",
      linewidth = 0.6,
      colour = "#3B78B4"
    ) +
    geom_errorbar(
      aes(xmin = lower_ci, xmax = upper_ci, colour = excludes_zero),
      orientation = "y",
      width = 0.12,
      linewidth = 0.55
    ) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = excludes_zero), size = 3) +
    geom_text(
      aes(
        label = format_rating_difference(difference),
        colour = excludes_zero
      ),
      nudge_y = 0.3,
      vjust = 0.5,
      size = 30 / ggplot2::.pt
    ) +
    scale_colour_manual(
      values = c(`FALSE` = "#222222", `TRUE` = "#D94B5B"),
      guide = "none"
    ) +
    scale_y_discrete(
      labels = function(x) unname(likert_display_labels[x]),
      expand = expansion(add = 0.5)
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = -2:2,
      labels = function(x) format_rating_difference(x),
      expand = expansion(mult = 0.04)
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(
      xlim = c(-likert_contrast_limit, likert_contrast_limit),
      clip = "on"
    ) +
    labs(
      title = unname(likert_panel_titles[question_name]),
      x = NULL,
      y = NULL
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_family = "Lato", base_size = 20) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        hjust = 0.5,
        face = "bold",
        size = 50
      ),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 20),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 40, margin = margin(r = 12)),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      axis.line.y = element_blank(),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      plot.margin = margin(6, 12, 8, 12)
    )

  if (!show_x) {
    p <- p +
      theme(
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
      )
  }

  if (!show_labels) {
    p <- p +
      theme(axis.text.y = element_blank())
  }

  p
}
```

Intervals are Dunnett-adjusted 95% confidence intervals (exact multivariate-t adjustment; family = the six contrasts against Basic within each item). Red marks intervals that exclude zero.](../figures/likert_contrast_figure.png)

```{r likert-contrast-summary}
#| include: false
likert_contrast_sentence <- function(question_name) {
  rows <- likert_contrasts |>
    filter(question == question_name, excludes_zero) |>
    arrange(desc(difference))
  if (nrow(rows) == 0) {
    return("no visualization differs from Basic topoplot")
  }
  paste(
    sprintf(
      "%s (%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f])",
      unname(likert_display_labels[as.character(rows$vistype)]),
      rows$difference, rows$lower_ci, rows$upper_ci
    ),
    collapse = "; "
  )
}

likert_sensitivity <- likert_contrasts |>
  mutate(question = as.character(question), vistype = as.character(vistype)) |>
  inner_join(likert_lmm_contrasts, by = c("question", "vistype")) |>
  mutate(
    lmm_excludes_zero = lmm_lower > 0 | lmm_upper < 0,
    agree = excludes_zero == lmm_excludes_zero
  )
```

**Contrasts against Basic topoplot** (Dunnett-adjusted 95% CIs; only intervals that exclude
zero are listed):

`r paste0("- ", question_columns, ": ", purrr::map_chr(question_columns, likert_contrast_sentence), ".", collapse = "\n")`

Differences between the uncertainty visualizations themselves were not tested, so the page
does not name a best visualization for any item.

::: {.callout-note title="Sensitivity: linear mixed model on the 1–5 ratings" collapse="true"}
```{r likert-lmm-sensitivity}
likert_sensitivity |>
  mutate(
    vistype = unname(likert_display_labels[vistype]),
    clmm = sprintf("%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f]", difference, lower_ci, upper_ci),
    lmm = sprintf("%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f]", lmm_difference, lmm_lower, lmm_upper),
    agree = if_else(agree, "yes", "**no**")
  ) |>
  select(question, vistype, clmm, lmm, agree) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    col.names = c(
      "Evaluation criterion", "Visualization vs Basic",
      "Ordinal model (CLMM)", "Linear mixed model", "Same conclusion"
    ),
    caption = paste(
      "Dunnett-adjusted differences vs Basic topoplot from the ordinal model and",
      "from a linear mixed model <code>rating ~ vistype + (1 | ID)</code>"
    ),
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )
```

The two models agree on whether the interval excludes zero for
`r sum(likert_sensitivity$agree)` of `r nrow(likert_sensitivity)` contrasts.
:::

```{r likert-quality-sensitivity}
#| include: false
source(project_path("scripts", "data_quality.R"))

likert_contrasts_screened <- likert_model_data |>
  filter(!as.integer(as.character(ID)) %in% flagged_ids) |>
  mutate(ID = droplevels(ID)) |>
  (\(data) split(data, data$question))() |>
  imap_dfr(function(data_question, question_name) {
    fit <- clmm(rating_ord ~ vistype + (1 | ID), data = data_question, Hess = TRUE)
    question_emmeans <- emmeans(fit, ~ vistype, mode = "mean.class")
    set.seed(20261118)  # adjust = "mvt" integrates numerically (Monte Carlo)
    contrast(
      question_emmeans,
      method = "trt.vs.ctrl",
      ref = which(question_emmeans@levels$vistype == "basic"),
      adjust = "mvt"
    ) |>
      confint() |>
      as.data.frame() |>
      transmute(
        question = question_name,
        vistype = stringr::str_remove(contrast, " - basic$"),
        screened_difference = estimate,
        screened_lower = asymp.LCL,
        screened_upper = asymp.UCL
      )
  })

likert_quality_sensitivity <- likert_contrasts |>
  mutate(question = as.character(question), vistype = as.character(vistype)) |>
  inner_join(likert_contrasts_screened, by = c("question", "vistype")) |>
  mutate(
    shift = screened_difference - difference,
    screened_excludes_zero = screened_lower > 0 | screened_upper < 0,
    agree = excludes_zero == screened_excludes_zero
  )
```

**Sensitivity: quality screen.** Without the `r length(flagged_ids)` participants flagged
for speeding or straight-lining (see the [Quality control](quality.qmd) page), the contrasts against Basic move by at
most `r sprintf("%.2f", max(abs(likert_quality_sensitivity$shift)))` scale points, and
`r sum(!likert_quality_sensitivity$agree)` of `r nrow(likert_quality_sensitivity)` intervals
change their position relative to zero.


```{r}
likert_estimates |>
  mutate(
    ci_width = upper_ci - lower_ci,
    lower_half = estimated_rating - lower_ci,
    upper_half = upper_ci - estimated_rating
  ) |>
  arrange(question, vistype) |>
  mutate(vistype = table_vistype(vistype)) |>
  select(
    question,
    vistype,
    estimated_rating,
    lower_ci,
    upper_ci,
    ci_width,
    lower_half,
    upper_half
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 2,
    col.names = c(
      "Evaluation criterion",
      "Visualization type",
      "Estimated rating",
      "Lower 95% CI",
      "Upper 95% CI",
      "CI width",
      "Distance to lower bound",
      "Distance to upper bound"
    ),
    caption = "Confidence-interval diagnostics for estimated ratings",
    table.attr = kable_table_attributes
  )

model_table_note(paste0(
  "Separate cumulative-link mixed models with logit link are fitted for each ",
  "evaluation criterion: <code>rating_ord ~ vistype + (1 | ID)</code>. ",
  "The displayed interval widths and distances are calculated from the same ",
  "expected-rating estimates and their asymptotic pointwise 95% confidence intervals."
))
```
